units.title: Unit 19 — Socialising and networking
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition); printed pages 44–45 (PDF pages 46–47).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition)
units.category: Leisure and lifestyle · social events, business networking and social expressions
learningObjectives: Name social events, distinguish wedding ceremonies, receptions and pre-wedding parties in British English.
Contrast socialising with professional networking and apply the appropriate register.
Use informal expressions for social groups, status, romantic relationships and missed dates accurately.

sectionsChecked: Exercises 19.1–19.3, reflection task 19.4, and answer key

items.pt: festa de inauguração de casa nova
items.example: They invited their neighbours to a housewarming shortly after moving in.
items.note: A party celebrating a move into a new home; housewarming party is also common.

items.example: The groom chose a quiet stag party rather than a weekend abroad.
items.note: Mainly British English for a pre-wedding party associated with the groom; stag do and stag night are alternatives.

items.example: Her friends arranged a hen night before the wedding.
items.note: Mainly British English for a pre-wedding event associated with the bride; hen party or hen do are also used.

items.example: Guests were asked to wear fancy dress to the charity event.
items.note: In British English, costumes for a themed party; US English often says costume party.

items.pt: grupo de pessoas que participam diretamente da cerimônia de casamento
items.example: The wedding party gathered for photographs before the guests arrived.
items.note: The close group directly involved in a wedding, not necessarily everybody attending the reception.

items.example: The organisers held a reception for international visitors after the ceremony.
items.note: A formal gathering; a wedding reception specifically follows a wedding ceremony.

items.pt: festa ou recepção após o casamento
items.example: The wedding reception was held in a small venue overlooking the lake.
items.note: The social celebration after the ceremony; distinct from the wedding party as a group of people.

items.pt: baile formal promovido por uma empresa
items.example: The company ball brought together employees from several regional offices.
items.note: A ball is a formal social event, often with dancing; not a sports event.

items.example: The awards dinner was a black-tie event, so everyone dressed formally.
items.note: Usually requires formal evening wear; black-tie is conventionally hyphenated before a noun.

items.example: The publishers organised a launch party for the new novel.
items.note: A celebration of a new product, book or other public release.

items.pt: noite de lazer só entre amigas
items.example: They planned a girls’ night out to celebrate finishing their exams.
items.note: Informal expression for an evening out with female friends; often used by adults as well.

items.pt: festa de despedida de alguém que está saindo de uma empresa
items.example: We organised a leaving do for a colleague who was moving abroad.
items.note: Informal British English; do is a casual noun for a party or social event.

items.example: His stag night was a small gathering with close friends.
items.note: British alternative to stag party; highlighted by the unit exercise.

items.example: The bride wanted a relaxed hen party with a few friends.
items.note: British alternative to hen night or hen do; highlighted by the unit exercise.

items.example: Everyone brought a costume to the fancy-dress party.
items.note: In British English, this is a costume party, not a party where guests wear elegant clothes.

items.pt: criação e manutenção de contatos profissionais
items.example: Networking helped her meet researchers from other institutions.
items.note: Building useful professional connections, not simply socialising for pleasure.

items.example: Socialising after the conference helped the new team feel more comfortable.
items.note: Spending time with people for enjoyment; distinguish it from purposeful career networking.

items.example: The delegates exchanged business cards before the panel discussion.
items.note: Exchange normally suggests that both people give and receive something.

items.pt: marcar um almoço; almoçar juntos para conversar
items.example: We should do lunch sometime and talk about the project.
items.note: Informal, sometimes associated with business or social networking; more casual than arrange a business lunch.

items.pt: conviver ou circular com pessoas influentes
items.example: He began hobnobbing with senior executives after his promotion.
items.note: Often implies socialising with influential people for status or advantage; may sound disapproving.

items.pt: conviver ou estar lado a lado com pessoas conhecidas ou influentes
items.example: At the festival, young directors rubbed shoulders with established stars.
items.note: Informal idiom for mixing socially with famous, important or influential people.

items.example: The event was an opportunity to make contacts in the publishing industry.
items.note: In networking, contacts are people who may be professionally useful.

items.example: She prepared questions rather than leaving the meeting to chance.
items.note: Used when somebody avoids planning and relies on luck instead.

items.example: A proactive employee raises potential issues before they become serious.
items.note: Taking the initiative rather than merely reacting to events.

items.example: He usually hangs out with his former classmates at weekends.
items.note: Informal phrasal verb for spending leisure time with people.

items.example: When she was younger, she knocked around with a group of musicians.
items.note: Informal British alternative to hang out with; typically refers to a group of acquaintances.

items.pt: ficar tempo demais na casa ou evento de alguém
items.example: We thanked our hosts and left before we could outstay our welcome.
items.note: Stay beyond the point when a host is pleased to have you; your can change to my, his, etc.

items.pt: festeiro inveterado; pessoa que adora festas
items.example: Although she works long hours, she is a party animal at weekends.
items.note: Informal and often humorous description of someone who loves parties.

items.pt: fechado em panelinhas; que exclui quem é de fora
items.example: The club felt rather cliquey to newcomers.
items.note: Disapproving adjective for a group or environment dominated by exclusive circles.

items.example: A small clique made most of the decisions without consulting the others.
items.note: Disapproving noun for an exclusive group; the final -que is not pronounced.

items.example: She introduced me to her crowd at the concert.
items.note: Informal sense meaning someone’s circle of friends; not necessarily a large audience.

items.example: Rumours began when the two actors were seen together repeatedly, but they were not an item.
items.note: Informal expression meaning two people are in a romantic relationship.

items.pt: dar um bolo em alguém; faltar a um encontro marcado
items.example: I waited at the cafe for an hour because my date stood me up.
items.note: Fail to turn up for an arranged meeting, typically a date; often used with a personal object.

units.title: Unit 20 — The performance arts: reviews and critiques
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition); printed pages 46–47 (PDF pages 48–49).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition)
units.category: Leisure and lifestyle · performing arts, criticism, reviews and auditions
learningObjectives: Distinguish nuanced adjectives used to review artistic work, including emotional force, credibility and originality.
Describe critical acclaim and failure with precise collocations and industry vocabulary.
Use vocabulary for auditions, rehearsals and artistic interpretation in natural contexts.
Recognise suspense and film-industry terms appearing in reviews.

sectionsChecked: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances, including Language help
Exercises 20.1–20.4, reflection task 20.5, and answer key

items.pt: superestimado; mais elogiado do que merece
items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The series was overrated in my view, despite its impressive cast.
items.note: Not as good as its reputation suggests; opposite of underrated.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The script relied on a hackneyed story about a misunderstood genius.
items.note: Describes a phrase, idea or plot used so often that it seems stale or unoriginal.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The documentary was disjointed, jumping between unrelated interviews.
items.note: Parts are not linked smoothly or logically; contrast coherent.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The ending was so far-fetched that it undermined the whole thriller.
items.note: Implausible, even if imaginative; not simply fictional.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The comedian included a few risqué jokes in the late-night show.
items.note: Suggestive or liable to offend conventional standards, often in sexual matters; typically qualified by a bit or rather.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The final episode was gripping without relying on special effects.
items.note: Strongly holds an audience’s attention through suspense or excitement.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The film offered a harrowing account of families displaced by war.
items.note: Emotionally painful or distressing, usually due to a disturbing subject; not merely exciting.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The final scene was moving because it showed a quiet act of forgiveness.
items.note: Creates strong tender or sad emotions; not the same as movement in a physical sense.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The violinist gave a memorable performance at the festival.
items.note: Worth remembering because it is striking or special; can be positive or negative depending on context.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The dancers created an unforgettable finale with almost no scenery.
items.note: So striking that it is hard to forget; often stronger than memorable.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: Her understated performance made the character’s grief more believable.
items.note: Deliberately restrained rather than exaggerated; frequently complimentary in reviews.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The unnecessarily long introduction made the play tedious.
items.note: Boring because something is lengthy, repetitive or slow; stronger than merely unexciting.

items.section: A · Useful adjectives for describing works and performances
items.example: The comic’s observations about office life were hilarious.
items.note: Extremely funny, not merely cheerful or pleasant.

items.example: Deafening applause greeted the orchestra after the last movement.
items.note: Deafening intensifies the noise and strength of audience approval.

items.example: The debut production received glowing reviews from several newspapers.
items.note: A glowing review expresses strong admiration and approval.

items.pt: bis; pedido para repetir ou apresentar mais uma música
items.example: The crowd called for an encore after the singer left the stage.
items.note: An additional performance given after applause; common collocations include call for and perform an encore.

items.example: The pianist received a standing ovation at the end of the recital.
items.note: Audience members stand to applaud; give or receive a standing ovation.

items.example: The composer accepted an award for her original soundtrack.
items.note: A formal prize or honour; award can also be a verb, as in award a prize.

items.example: An up-and-coming director was selected for the international festival.
items.note: Describes someone likely to become successful or prominent; used before a noun.

items.example: Critics considered the minimalist production a masterpiece of modern theatre.
items.note: An exceptionally good work of art, literature or performance.

items.pt: sempre escalado para o mesmo tipo de papel
items.example: The actor worried about being typecast as a villain after the successful series.
items.note: Repeatedly cast in similar roles because of appearance or previous performances; different from miscast.

items.example: Several reviewers panned the sequel for its weak dialogue.
items.note: In criticism, pan means review very unfavourably; not the kitchen utensil.

items.pt: detonar; criticar severamente (principalmente no inglês britânico)
items.example: The new stage adaptation was slated by several critics.
items.note: Informal British verb for strongly criticising a production; not the roofing material.

items.example: The director was widely lauded for her inventive staging.
items.note: Formal verb meaning praise highly; often appears as be lauded by/for.

items.pt: fracassar completamente (no palco ou nas bilheterias)
items.example: The comedy bombed when it opened, despite its famous lead.
items.note: Informal verb meaning fail badly as a performance or commercial release.

items.example: Some spectators booed the ending, although others applauded.
items.note: Express disapproval aloud, typically by shouting boo; contrast applause.

items.pt: fracasso; fiasco (de filme, peça ou show)
items.example: The expensive musical was a commercial flop and closed after a month.
items.note: Countable noun for a failed production; also a verb meaning fail.

items.example: The lead actor was miscast as a teenager despite an otherwise strong performance.
items.note: The wrong performer has been chosen for a role; unlike typecast, it need not be a repeated pattern.

items.example: The hero’s sudden change of heart felt unconvincing.
items.note: Not believable in an acting performance, argument or fictional event.

items.example: The soprano was universally lauded for her farewell concert.
items.note: Universally is a strong, often rhetorical intensifier suggesting virtually everyone praises it.

items.example: She prepared two monologues for the audition.
items.note: A trial performance to assess suitability for a part or role; also used for music.

items.pt: ensaio de peça, show ou apresentação
items.example: The cast stayed late for the final rehearsal before opening night.
items.note: Practice in preparation for a public performance; often do or attend rehearsals.

items.pt: interpretação artística; modo pessoal de executar uma obra
items.example: Her interpretation of the song sounded quieter and more reflective.
items.note: The performer’s understanding and delivery of a work; not necessarily its translation.

items.example: The audience preferred the original version to the modern arrangement.
items.note: The earlier or source performance; distinct from later adaptations or covers.

items.pt: regravação; versão de uma música de outro artista
items.example: The band recorded a cover version of a classic soul song.
items.note: A new performance of a song originally associated with another artist; cover is also used alone.

items.example: Her portrayal of the scientist avoided the usual stereotypes.
items.note: The way an actor depicts a character; can also describe literary or artistic representations.

items.pt: história ou final cheio de suspense
items.example: The season ended on a cliffhanger, leaving the main character’s fate uncertain.
items.note: A tense situation or ending whose outcome is unresolved; used here in a review headline.

items.pt: grande sucesso comercial, especialmente de bilheteria
items.example: The studio released a summer blockbuster with an enormous marketing budget.
items.note: A hugely successful or heavily promoted mass-market film or entertainment release.

items.example: The festival offered a showcase for budding playwrights.
items.note: Used before nouns for people beginning to show a talent or career potential.

items.pt: policial de ação com policiais e criminosos
items.example: The festival included a lively cops-and-robbers thriller from the 1970s.
items.note: Informal compound modifier for a story involving police and criminals; cops is informal.

items.word: keep you on the edge of your seat
items.pt: deixar você na ponta da cadeira; prender a atenção com suspense
items.example: The final act kept us on the edge of our seats.
items.note: Idiom for sustained suspense or excitement; pronouns can change, and seats often becomes plural.

items.example: The director’s new production is not to be missed.
items.note: Enthusiastic recommendation common in headlines and promotional reviews.

items.example: His accent was convincing enough to make the role believable.
items.note: Credible or persuasive; opposite of unconvincing in reviews of acting.
